$comment: Pre-registration of the change-impact measurement (#582, epic #572). Version 5 changes ONLY the population: the repository, the commit range and the sample. Arms, thresholds, both verdicts, the truth definition and the context metric are carried over from version 4 unchanged and were fixed before any bastra-io scenario was mined. Supersedes code-awareness-roi.json registration_version 3, which is kept as the record of the completed v3 run and stays reproducible from ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 with evaluate.mjs. Thresholds decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18. Fixed BEFORE any v4 scenario has been run; the two pilot commits named under sample.excluded_pilot were run against the plumbing only and are excluded from the sample. Amending anything after the main run has started invalidates that run: bump registration_version and say which version a report belongs to.
registered_by: Claude Opus 5; thresholds decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18
supersedes: code-awareness-roi.json registration_version 3; and registration_version 4 of this file, which named bastra-recall as the population
why_a_new_registration: v3 answered its question and the answer invalidated its own comparison: `find_code` was offered in 44 of 44 runs and called in 0, so both arms ran the same grep behaviour and the measured difference (+0.8 Pp recall) is noise between two runs of one procedure. Two things were confounded — whether an agent REACHES for the graph, and whether the graph's answer HELPS. This design separates them into three arms.
question: (a) Adoption: offered a change-impact tool described graph-first, how often does an agent call it? (b) Effect: when the change-impact answer is in front of the agent, does it name more of the files the change really breaks, without naming more wrong ones and without costing disproportionate context?

A.name: grep
A.description: No MCP server at all — text search and file reads only. Identical to v3's control arm.

B.name: offered
B.description: `find_code` and `find_affected_files` offered over stdio MCP, nothing else changed. Whether the agent calls them is the observation.

prefilled.name: prefilled
prefilled.description: The same tools, plus the `find_affected_files` answer for exactly the planned change already in the prompt. The information is guaranteed to have been SHOWN; nothing forces the agent to use it, which is why the arm is not called `forced`.
prefilled.symbols_from: the product's own `changedSymbolsOf` applied to the scenario diff — not a hand-written list, so both graph arms start from the information the prompt already carries

arms.mcp_server: packages/eval/code-roi/v2/code-tools-mcp.mjs (the product's own tool definitions, handlers AND server instructions — an arm served without the instructions measures a weaker surface than any real user is given)

frozen_surface.$comment: What arm B is offered, pinned so a later edit cannot quietly change what was measured. Hashes are of the built artefacts (packages/daemon/dist). TUNED ON DEVELOPMENT DATA: the wording was arrived at over several rounds on the BURNED v3 scenarios of bastra-recall, never on a bastra-io scenario and never on the 7 fresh bastra-recall ones. The adoption threshold therefore tests it on unseen data, which is the only reason a tuned description may be measured at all.
frozen_surface.conditional: The code paragraph is appended only when the user has code awareness on (`serverInstructions(enabled)`), because without a graph both tools answer `unavailable` and an instruction pointing at them would spend its trust for nothing. An arm served a graph gets it; a user without one never sees it.

development_result.baseline: 0/44 (v3) and 0/2 (v4 pilot) — the instructions named no code tool at all
development_result.frozen_memory_first: 3/5 on the first burned set, 5/5 on the second — 8/10 overall
development_result.rejected_code_first: 5/5 and 5/5, with the code paragraph LEADING ('CODE FIRST')
development_result.decision: The memory-first version is the one frozen and measured, although it adopts less on development data. bastra-recall is the memory first, and these instructions reach every client — including users with no code and no graph. Product before measured value; the difference is recorded here so the adoption result can be read with it in view.
development_result.$comment: Development data throughout: it says the mechanism works on the cases it was built against, not that it generalises.

frozen_surface.known_harness_deviation: In real Claude Code an MCP tool is regularly DEFERRED — its schema is not loaded and the client fetches it first. This harness (`--strict-mcp-config`, few tools) loads them immediately, so a tool search returns EMPTY, which agents read as 'the tool is missing' before the clause addressed it. Arm B therefore measures a slightly easier surface than a real session on the loading step, and a slightly harder one on nothing. Not corrected: making the harness defer tools is not something the runner can set.

arms.isolation: unchanged from v3: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence`, a fresh process per scenario and arm, cwd a throwaway worktree with no `.git`, the graph moved out of the tree so no arm can read it as a file
arms.tools: Read and read-only shell search; no edits, no subagents, no web
arms.arm_order: randomized per scenario by the registered seed, written into the scenario file before the first run

unit_and_truth.unit: one historical change to one file, at most one scenario per file
unit_and_truth.ground_truth: a file is affected when it carries a type error after applying exactly that file's diff that it did not carry before; errors compared as (file, TS code, message) multisets with line and column ignored; adjudicated by hand before any arm runs, removals only with a written reason
unit_and_truth.$comment: The truth definition is not touched. Changing the ruler and the tool in the same step would leave nothing comparable.

primary_metric.name: affected_file_recall
primary_metric.definition: Per scenario: |named ∩ truth| / |truth|, `named` being the JSON array on the last FILES: line of the final answer, normalized to repo-relative POSIX paths.
primary_metric.compared: prefilled against A, paired per scenario

context_metric.name: input_tokens
context_metric.definition: Per arm, from the run's own `result` event: modelUsage[claude-sonnet-5].inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens. All three are summed because a cached token is a token the model read. Side models the client calls on its own (haiku for titles and the like) are excluded — they are not the agent's context and differ between arms at random. Fallback when modelUsage is absent: the run-level `usage` block summed the same way, and the row is marked `usageFallback`.
context_metric.$comment: v3 counted characters of TOOL RESULTS. That rule is blind to the prompt, and the prefilled arm's block arrives in the prompt — under it the arm that spends the most context would have scored as free. This is the correction the v4 design needs to be honest about its own cost.

verdicts.$comment: TWO verdicts, decided separately, with no combined status. Decided by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18. A tool nobody calls whose answer would have helped, and a tool everyone calls whose answer does not, are opposite findings needing opposite work — one word covering both would hide which it was. Each verdict is pass, fail, underpowered (fewer than min_scenarios) or not_evaluable.

adoption.question: Does an agent offered the tool call it?

effect.question: Does the answer, once shown, make the agent name more of the breaking files without more wrong ones and without disproportionate context?
effect.$comment: All four of these must hold for the effect verdict to pass; none of them touches the adoption verdict.

thresholds.$comment: Decided by Daniel Nevoigt, 2026-09-18. Grouped into the two verdicts above; the numbers are unchanged from the first registration of this design.
thresholds.$comment_adoption: In arm B, at least 70 % of scenarios must call `find_affected_files` at least once. `find_code` calls are reported but do NOT count towards this: an agent that locates a symbol has not asked what breaks.
thresholds.$comment_recall: Mean paired difference prefilled − A of at least 5 percentage points, AND the lower bound of its 95 % bootstrap interval above 0.
thresholds.$comment_precision: Mean paired difference in precision (prefilled − A) not below −0.05.
thresholds.$comment_context: On scenarios solved in BOTH arms (recall ≥ 0.8), median prefilled input tokens at most 1.25 × median A. The restriction to scenarios both arms solved is INHERITED from registration 3, where its reason is recorded: cost is compared only where both got the answer, so a cheap wrong answer cannot win on cost. The unfiltered ratio over every scenario is reported alongside it as `notGated.context_ratio_all_scenarios`.

not_gated.context_ratio_all_scenarios: The context ratio over every scenario, not just the ones both arms solved. Reported, never gated.
not_gated.b_vs_a: Arm B against arm A is reported and never gated: it multiplies adoption and effect, and an agent that never calls the tool makes B identical to A. Reporting it as the effect is what made the v3 report unreadable.
not_gated.latency_and_hook_block: Both stay with registration 3 and come from lane telemetry (`bastra logs --stats`), not from these runs.

population.$comment: CHANGED IN VERSION 5, and the only thing that changed. bastra-recall cannot supply this sample: its history is exhausted. 369 commits before the v3 range end yield 694 candidate file changes, 11 qualifying, 7 after the freshness exclusions — and ZERO of those 7 break across a package boundary, which is exactly the mechanism #582 added. Measuring cross-package impact on a sample with no cross-package breaks would measure nothing.
population.repository_path: /Users/n0mad/Projekte/bastra-io (local clone; never written to — the miner reads with `git archive` and extracts into ~/.bastra/eval, and creates no git worktree in it)
population.why_this_repository: The only other local repository that is a TypeScript monorepo with real cross-package imports: a pnpm workspace of 17 packages under scope @bastra, 237 imports of @bastra/* from the app, 194 non-merge commits, 452 TS/TSX files. Verified before mining: an archived tree typechecks with 0 errors, and a mutation to one exported function in packages/db surfaces 16 new type errors in apps/bastra-io — the cross-package breakage class the bastra-recall sample lacked entirely.

candidates_considered.verdict: no workspace packages, so no package boundary to measure
in the repository but outside the typechecked graph; changes there produce no truth
pnpm workspace, but 2 commits — no history

population.privacy: Only repository name, commit ids and file paths are recorded outside ~/.bastra/eval. No source content from bastra-io appears in this registration or in BEFUND.md; transcripts and archives stay local. Checked before mining: the tree carries no secrets or customer data (one .env.example, no keys, no customer files).
population.truth_mechanics: bastra-io has ONE tsconfig (apps/bastra-io) and its packages are consumed as raw TS source (`main: ./src/index.ts`), so one typecheck covers the app plus every package source it reaches; bastra-recall needed one per package plus a build of core first. Both are derived from the repository's own manifests by `repo-profile.mjs` — the truth DEFINITION is unchanged, only the command that produces it.

sample.$comment_fresh: bastra-io has never been used to develop this tooling; the whole repository is unseen data. The one product change made while looking at it (pnpm-workspace.yaml support in workspace-packages.ts) was derived from the repository's LAYOUT, not from any scenario, and no scenario informed a threshold or a query parameter. The frozen parameters — the package-import narrowing threshold of 20, the specific-entry preference, the file-count cap — are unchanged from the bastra-recall work and were not touched here.
sample.commit_range: non-merge commits reachable from bastra-io HEAD at mining time, walked NEWEST first, `mine-repo.mjs --stop-at 45`
sample.miner: packages/eval/code-roi/v2/mine-repo.mjs (archive-based; `mine.mjs` remains the bastra-recall miner and is untouched)

excluded_pilot.$comment: The two bastra-recall pilot scenarios of version 4. They are in a different repository and cannot appear in this sample; kept here so the exclusion survives if bastra-recall is ever mined again.
excluded_pilot.enforced_by: select.mjs drops any candidate from these commits before writing the scenario file.

pooling.$comment: Released by Daniel Nevoigt on 2026-09-18, before any arm ran: no single local repository supplies 40 scenarios with a usable share of cross-package breaks. The populations differ in package layout, typecheck granularity and size, so the pooled mean is reported WITH a per-repository breakdown — and the breakdown is descriptive, never gated. Every scenario carries its own `repo`, so any row can be re-run and re-scored on its own.
pooling.$comment_order: FIXED HERE, before mining, so the pool cannot be assembled to suit the result. Repositories are drawn in this order until min_scenarios is reached; bastra-io first because it is the one with cross-package structure.
pooling.per_repo_rules: identical for every repository: the same unit, the same truth definition, the same inclusion caps, the same one-scenario-per-file rule. A repository is mined by `mine-repo.mjs` with its own profile; nothing per repository is tuned.
pooling.$comment_used_only_when_short: AMENDED 2026-09-19, before any arm ran and before the registration was committed: pooling and its cap apply only when the FIRST repository alone does not reach min_scenarios. As first written the cap of 30 was unconditional, which would have cut a sufficient single-repository sample (bastra-io mined 40) down to 30 and then declared it underpowered — a rule that fires where there is no pooling and therefore no domination to prevent. The cap's purpose is unchanged: it bounds one repository's share OF A POOLED sample.
pooling.$comment_cap: In a pooled sample, at most 30 scenarios from any one repository, so none carries more than three quarters of a 40-scenario sample. A repository that could supply more is cut off at the cap in walk order — the cut is the tail, never a choice among its scenarios.
pooling.file_identity: The one-scenario-per-file rule applies per repository, keyed by repo + path: `packages/db/src/index.ts` in two repositories are two different files.
pooling.reporting: The report carries the pooled verdicts plus, for each repository, its n, recall, precision and adoption — reported for completeness, gated never.

sample.$comment_size: 40 independent changes. Fewer qualifying → the report says `underpowered` (18.1) for both verdicts, not a verdict.

statistics.method: paired bootstrap, 10 000 resamples, resampling by changed file with replacement

run_conditions.per_scenario_base: the commit's parent SHA, recorded in the scenario file with the graph's sha256
run_conditions.$comment_ceiling: Raised by Daniel from 20 to 40 $ on 18.09.2026, before the run.
run_conditions.cost_estimate: From the v4 pilot on bastra-recall (6 arms, $0.9919, mean $0.1653 per arm, mean 157 168 input tokens per arm): 3 arms x $0.1653 = $0.496 per scenario, so 40 scenarios = $19.84 and 45 = $22.32. Both sit under the $40 ceiling, which leaves room for the larger prompts a pooled sample may carry. The runner stops BEFORE the arm that would cross the ceiling, not after.
run_conditions.$comment_cost: Enforced by the runner, not documented at it: every finished arm's `total_cost_usd` is summed and the next arm only starts while the ceiling is still out of reach at the running average cost per arm. Raising it is a decision, not a flag someone reaches for at 2 a.m. (CODE_ROI_COST_CEILING).
run_conditions.frozen_archive: ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 is never written by a v4 script — `archive.mjs` refuses it, because the v3 report is only reproducible while that archive is untouched.

archive.location: the directory named by CODE_ROI_OUT for the run
contents: scenario file with base SHAs, arm order and seed
raw stream-json transcript of every arm run
the prefilled block handed to the third arm, per scenario

reporting_duties: Adoption from arm B, with its N, separately for find_affected_files and find_code.
Effect from prefilled against A: paired mean with its 95 % interval, and the per-scenario rows.
Precision and context (input tokens) as defined above.
B against A, labelled as adoption and effect combined, never as the effect.
The cost of the run against the ceiling.
That the offline figures on the v3 sample (recall 91.3 %, precision 52.4 %) are development data and carry no weight here.
Both verdicts separately — adoption and effect — and never a combined status.
An honest `underpowered` / `not_evaluable` per 18.1 where the sample does not support a verdict.
The registration_version the report belongs to.
$comment_failure: A missed threshold is recorded as the finding; thresholds are not moved afterwards.
